records.subject: FireRed Pokemon League timed BG-palette lighting sequences (Elite Four 12 palettes, Champion room 9 palettes)

verification.fact: tables: sEliteFourLightingPalettes (L2081, 12 x 16-colour), sChampionRoomLightingPalettes (L2096, 9 x 16-colour), sEliteFourLightingTimers (L2108) = [40, 12, 12, 12, 12, 12, 12, 12, 12, 12, 12], sChampionRoomLightingTimers (L2122) = [20, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8]

step counts: Elite Four loops palettes 0-10 (data[2]=11; 160 ticks per cycle = one 40-tick hold + ten 12-tick steps); Champion room loops palettes 0-7 (data[2]=8; 76 ticks per cycle = one 20-tick hold + seven 8-tick steps). The last palette of each set (E4 #11, Champion #8) has no timer and is never in the loop; it is the settled stop state

timer: DoPokemonLeagueLightingEffect (L2133) creates a priority-8 task and loads palette 0; Task_RunPokemonLeagueLightingEffect (L2160) decrements data[0] per frame and at 0 advances data[1] (wrapping), reloads timer and palette. It ticks only while no palette fade is active, FLAG_TEMP_2 (player has entered) is set, FLAG_TEMP_5 (battle running) is clear and the quest-log grayscale tint is off

slot/range: LoadPalette(..., BG_PLTT_ID(7), PLTT_SIZE_4BPP) = one 16-colour BG palette, then ApplyGlobalTintToPaletteSlot(7, 1) every step. Across palettes only colour indices [3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15] change, identical index set in both rooms

start/stop/final: started per room from MAP_SCRIPT_ON_RESUME via PokemonLeague_EventScript_DoLightingEffect (data/scripts/pokemon_league.inc L62); if FLAG_TEMP_3 (room cleared) is already set it becomes Task_CancelPokemonLeagueLightingEffect (L2187), which waits for FLAG_TEMP_4 (door open), loads the stop-state palette, re-tints and destroys itself; StopPokemonLeagueLightingEffectTask (L2205) kills the loop task and is called from src/start_menu.c:453 and five sites in src/item_use.c

evidence.summary: Tables, timers, step counts, palette slot, changed colour indices and start/stop/final-state flow read from source and the 21 .pal files (JASC, 16 colours each). Platinum-side native mechanisms checked.

records.subject: FireRed Deoxys triangle: variable-driven staged palette feedback on an interactable object (generic half of a split finding)

split.reason: the generic idea (progress variable -> palette stage, re-derived on return to field) is separable from the Birth Island puzzle and rock choreography

verification.fact: state: VAR_DEOXYS_INTERACTION_NUM (0-10) is the stage; Task_DoDeoxysTriangleInteraction (L2365) reads it with VAR_DEOXYS_INTERACTION_STEP_COUNTER (incremented by IncrementBirthIslandRockStepCount, L2438, only on the Birth Island map): if steps since last touch exceed sDeoxysStepCaps[stage-1] the stage resets to 0 (result 0); at stage 10 FLAG_SYS_DEOXYS_AWAKENED is set (result 2); otherwise stage+1 (result 1); already awakened returns 3

palette-state: sDeoxysObjectPals (L2319, 11 palettes) loaded by MoveDeoxysObject (L2405) into OBJ_PLTT_ID(10), PLTT_SIZEOF(4) = 4 colours, then ApplyGlobalFieldPaletteTint(10). Only colour indices [0, 1, 2, 3] differ: grey -> warm orange glow ramp (stage 0 (139,139,139) -> stage 10 (255,205,156) on index 3)

restore: SetDeoxysTrianglePalette (L2451) reloads the palette for the current stage; run by BirthIsland_Exterior MAP_SCRIPT_ON_RETURN_TO_FIELD (data/maps/BirthIsland_Exterior/scripts.inc L8), so battle/menu returns keep the visible stage

persistence scope: VAR_DEOXYS_INTERACTION_NUM and the step counter are zeroed in MAP_SCRIPT_ON_TRANSITION (L15) and FLAG_SYS_DEOXYS_AWAKENED is cleared on each visit unless Deoxys already fled: the stage is save-block variable state but scoped to the visit, not long-term progression
